sentences.text: So, when the defendants have disputed the possession, identification and alleged ownership of the plaintiff over the property in dispute, then in a suit for bare injunction though title is corollary to the lawful possession over the property in question, but it is equally settled under Section 101 of Evidence Act that burden lies on the plaintiff to prove his case on the basis of material available, as such he cannot rely on weaknesses or absence of defence of defendants to discharge the onus.

In such circumstances, again burden lies upon the plaintiff to show that he is in unlawful possession of the suit schedule property as on the date of the suit and defendants interfered with his possession.

This being the fact, the plaintiff cannot contend that he is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property as on the date of the suit, as such though it is alleged that defendants made an attempt to interfere with the peaceful possession of the suit schedule property, but in view of the discussion made supra, the plaintiff failed to prove lawful possession and alleged obstruction as stated in the plaint.
